ayahs.1: O you wrapped in your cloak—
ayahs.4: Keep your garments—and yourself—pure from what defiles.
ayahs.5: Turn away from idols and everything that rivals Allah.
ayahs.6: Do not give expecting more in return.
ayahs.7: Endure with sabr—steadfast endurance—for the sake of your Rabb.
ayahs.9: that Day will be brutally hard—
ayahs.10: not easy for those who reject the truth.
ayahs.11: Leave to Me the one I created alone,
ayahs.13: with sons always at his side,
ayahs.14: and a life made smooth and comfortable—
ayahs.16: No—for he has been stubborn against Our signs.
ayahs.17: I will make his path steep and crushing.
ayahs.19: damned be him—how evil was what he decided!
ayahs.20: Damned again—how evil was what he decided!
ayahs.22: These opening letters—known as the muqatta'at—are among the signs whose full meaning Allah kept with Himself. They open the surah by reminding the reader that this Book is from beyond human authorship: approach it with humility, not arrogance.
ayahs.24: and said, 'This is nothing but ancient magic.
ayahs.25: This is only the word of a man.'
ayahs.26: I will soon cast him into Saqar—
ayahs.27: and what will make you realize what Saqar is?
ayahs.28: It spares no one to live or die,
ayahs.30: Nineteen keepers are appointed over it.
ayahs.31: We have set only stern angels as wardens of the Fire. We made their number a test for those who reject the truth—so the People of the Book would be certain, believers would grow in iman, and neither group would doubt. Those with sickness in their hearts and those who reject the truth would ask, 'What does Allah mean by this number?' Thus Allah leaves astray whomever He wills and guides whomever He wills. None knows the armies of your Rabb except Him. This is only a reminder for humanity.
ayahs.32: No! By the moon and its cycles,
ayahs.33: and the night as it withdraws,
ayahs.34: and the dawn as it brightens—
ayahs.35: Hell is among the greatest catastrophes,
ayahs.37: for whoever among you chooses to advance or hang back.
ayahs.38: Every soul is held for what it earned,
ayahs.39: except the people of the right—
ayahs.40: who will be in Gardens, asking one another
ayahs.41: about the guilty. They will ask them:
ayahs.43: They will answer, 'We were not among those who prayed salah—the formal prayer—
ayahs.44: nor did we feed the poor.
ayahs.45: We indulged in falsehood with those who indulged,
ayahs.46: and we denied the Day of Reckoning
ayahs.48: So the pleas of intercessors will not help them.
ayahs.49: What is wrong with them that they turn away from the Reminder?
ayahs.50: As if they were frightened wild donkeys
ayahs.51: These opening letters—known as the muqatta'at—are among the signs whose full meaning Allah kept with Himself. They open the surah by reminding the reader that this Book is from beyond human authorship: approach it with humility, not arrogance.
ayahs.52: Each of them wishes a personal letter from Allah were opened for all to read.
ayahs.53: No—they do not fear the Akhirah—the life after death.
ayahs.55: So let whoever wills be mindful of it.
ayahs.56: They cannot do so unless Allah wills. He alone is worthy of reverence and entitled to forgive.
